json.title: SlaEscalationRecordsETL drops tenant_id in gold projection
json.body:
## Problem

`SlaEscalationRecordsETL` does not carry `tenant_id` through to the gold layer, so downstream consumers that filter by tenant cannot query `gold/sla_escalation_records`.

The gold layer uses an explicit `select(...)` that lists only `id`, `case_id`, `notified_at`, `notified_at_ts`, `sla_state`, `ingested_at_ts`, `source_file_path` — [`Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py` lines 79-87](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py#L79-L87). `tenant_id` is not projected, so even when it is present in the source JSON and survives bronze/silver, it is dropped in gold.

Bronze does not explicitly cast `tenant_id` either — [lines 33-42](https://github.com/tazama-lf/biar/blob/main/automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py#L33-L42) — so its type is not normalised the way peer ETLs do it.

This diverges from the convention used by every other tenant-scoped ETL in the same directory (`CasesETL`, `TasksETL`, `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL`), which cast `tenant_id` as `string` in bronze and silver and re-select it in gold. See `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL.py` lines 36, 60, 86 for the pattern.

## Logs

Lakehouse Catalog notebook, after ODS was updated to emit `tenant_id`, the warehouse `sla_escalation_records` bronze/silver/gold layers were truncated, and the NiFi pipeline was reset and restarted:

```
ValueError                                Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[4], line 45
     43 t0  = time.time()
     44 # Load the authoritative Hudi table used by downstream metrics.
---> 45 cnt = load_tenant_hudi(path).count()
     46 elapsed = time.time() - t0

Cell In[1], line 12, in load_tenant_hudi(path, **options)
     10 tenant_col = next((c for c in TENANT_FILTER_COLUMNS if c in df.columns), None)
     11 if tenant_col is None:
---> 12     raise ValueError(
     13         f"Hudi table at {path} has no tenant filter column; "
     14         f"expected one of {TENANT_FILTER_COLUMNS}"
     15     )

ValueError: Hudi table at /opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/sla_escalation_records has no tenant filter column; expected one of ('tenant_id', 'tx_tenant_id', 'tenantid')
```

## Proposed solution

Update `automation-orchestrator/Table_ETLs/SlaEscalationRecordsETL.py` to match the tenant-carrying pattern already used by `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL`:

1. In `bronze()` (line 33-42): add `.withColumn(\"tenant_id\", F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\"))`.
2. In `silver()` (line 55-63): add `.withColumn(\"tenant_id\", F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\"))`.
3. In `gold()` `select(...)` (line 79-87): add `F.col(\"tenant_id\").cast(\"string\").alias(\"tenant_id\")`.

No schema changes required elsewhere — `tenant_id` is already emitted by NiFi from the ODS.

## Impact

- Lakehouse Catalog notebook cannot load `gold/sla_escalation_records`; the tenant filter step raises `ValueError` and downstream metrics dependent on this table fail.
- Any tenant-scoped query or view over SLA escalation records is blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gold/sla_escalation_records` contains a `tenant_id` column of type `string`.
- [ ] `silver/sla_escalation_records` and `bronze/sla_escalation_records` also contain `tenant_id`.
- [ ] `load_tenant_hudi(\"/opt/Tazama_Warehouse/gold/sla_escalation_records\")` returns a filtered DataFrame without raising.
- [ ] Behaviour matches `SlaEscalationThresholdsETL` for tenant column handling.
